title: Deacons and Gospel Origins
english: Concerning the writings for Timothy: Thaddaeus, Cleopas, and those with him. These are the names of the appointed deacons. First, Stephen the first martyr; second, Philip; third, Prochorus; fourth, Nicanor; fifth, Timon; sixth, Parmenas; and seventh, Nicholas. As for the leaders, who are these? Paul, Mark, Luke, Titus, Candace the eunuch, and John the Baptist.

It is necessary to know how the four gospels were written. After the ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ, the gospel according to Matthew was written after eight years, the one according to Mark after twelve years, the one according to Luke after fifteen years, and the one according to John after a hundred years during the reign of King Domitian. The gospel according to Matthew was written by him in the Hebrew dialect in Jerusalem and was given out, and it was interpreted by John. The one according to Mark was dictated by Peter in Rome. The one according to Luke was dictated by Paul in Rome. The one according to John was written on the island of Patmos and was dictated by John himself during the times of Trajan and Commodus. The one according to Luke was written by Luke, a disciple of the apostle Paul, of whom he himself makes mention.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG Appendices ad indices apostolorum discipulorumque u01-rem-early

title: The Authorship and Nature of the Gospels
english: An apostle writes in one epistle: Luke the beloved physician greets you, and the same evangelist composed the deeds of the holy apostles. It is not possible for these to be more or less in number.

For the Gospel according to John narrates the generation from the Father, its leading, practical, and glorious nature; in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God, and all things came through him; because of this, it is compared to the likeness of an eagle. But that according to Luke, being of a priestly character, began from Zacharias the priest, saying: It happened in the days of Herod, the king of the Jews, a certain priest named Zacharias of the division of Abia, since according to the tradition of the old law the priests served in turns; because of this, his appearance as calf-like is also related. But Matthew explains his generation according to man, the book...

title: The Gospel of Mark and Luke
english: Regarding the genesis of Jesus Christ, the son of Abraham, the birth of Jesus Christ was such that his gospel is likened to the anthropomorphic. Mark, however, made his beginning from the prophetic spirit descending from on high in the heavens, saying, 'The beginning of the gospel,' just as it is written in the prophets: 'A voice of one crying in the wilderness,' which is the prophetic image of the gospel; for this reason, he shows and recounts the icon of the lion in the wilderness: Holy Trinity, our God, save us by your grace. Mark the evangelist was bishop of the Alexandrians.

Luke the evangelist—these are the ones among the [?] who were scattered upon the preaching where the Lord said: 'If anyone does not eat my flesh and drink my blood, he is not worthy of me.' But the one through Peter and the one through Paul, having returned again to the Lord, are honored to evangelize for the sake of whom they also bore witness: the one having been burned, and the other having been crucified on an olive tree.
